proposals.hypothesis: LiCl is a wide-gap, Li-rich halide with no reducible cation, and its Cl- anion is hard to oxidize below about 4.4 V vs Li, so it should be stable against the 4.0 V LiCoO2 cathode. Halides such as LiCl are often reported as sulfide-compatible interlayers, and this family has not been sampled beyond LiF, which was penalized by reactions forming P/S/Ca products. A simple chloride tests whether a halide chemistry gives a lower contact penalty than the Li3BO3 borate, the best result so far.
proposals.motivation: Oxides, phosphates, silicates and LiF all gave contact penalties from P-, S- or Cl-containing reduction products (lowest so far Li3BO3 at about 0.29 eV/non-Li atom). The halide family, aside from LiF, is untested, and LiCl is a simple Li-rich candidate with a non-reducible cation.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (>2 eV), electronically insulating phosphate that is chemically robust toward both the 4.0 V LiCoO2 cathode and the sulfide electrolyte. Its PO4 framework is already fully oxidized, so it should carry a small interfacial redox penalty and act as a Li-conducting buffer layer, making it a strong first test in the phosphate family.

Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, fully oxidized, Li-rich oxide with Zr4+ in a stable octahedral framework. Its high Li2O content and the absence of a reducible P5+ or S-containing anion should make it less prone to the P2O5/SCl4-forming reaction seen with Li3PO4 against the sulfide electrolyte, and Zr4+ is hard to reduce at the sulfide interface. It is a known cathode coating that is chemically different from the phosphate tested first.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 gave a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom (bin 16) from reaction with Li6PS5Cl to form P2O5, SCl4, and SO2, so an oxide without a reducible central anion is the next logical family to test.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a wide-gap (~7 eV) ionic insulator with no reducible cation and a very electronegative F anion. It should be thermodynamically inert toward both the sulfide electrolyte (no P/S reduction products, unlike the Li3PO4 and Li2ZrO3 contacts) and the oxidized LiCoO2 surface at 4.0 V. It also gives a fluoride family test, which is chemically distinct from the phosphate and oxide candidates tried so far.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 and Li2ZrO3 both gave penalties from sulfur- and phosphorus-containing decomposition products against Li6PS5Cl (bins 28 and 16), so the next family to test is a fluoride that lacks a reducible central anion.

proposal.hypothesis: LiNbO3 is a wide-gap, fully oxidized Li-containing oxide with Nb5+ in a stable octahedral framework. Nb5+ is hard to reduce, and the niobate interface is known from sulfide-battery work to form only limited interphase products with Li6PS5Cl, unlike the P- and S-containing decomposition products seen for Li3PO4 and LiF. It is also a sufficiently wide-gap insulator to meet the band-gap and insulation requirements. This is a different chemistry from the phosphate, zirconate and fluoride tried so far.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (bin 28), Li2ZrO3 (bin 15) and LiF (bin 16) all showed contact penalties from sulfur- and phosphorus-containing products, so the next test is a Nb5+ oxide with a non-reducible cation.

proposal.hypothesis: LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, fully oxidized Li-rich oxide whose Al3+ is very hard to reduce. Al-O bonds are strong, and LiAlO2 is a widely used sulfide-compatible cathode coating, so it should avoid the P- and S-containing reduction products seen for Li3PO4, LiF and Li2ZrO3 against Li6PS5Cl.

The next test is an Al3+ oxide with a non-reducible cation, which is a different cation chemistry from the Zr, Nb and P candidates tried so far.
